Guardians win ALDS 2026

# Guardians erase 0-2 hole, complete ALDS comeback to punch ALCS ticket

October 11th, 2026

Tim Stebbins

CLEVELAND -- Guardians players, coaches, staff and front-office members gathered in the middle of the red-tinted home clubhouse at Progressive Field on Saturday night, forming a circle around manager Stephen Vogt. Before the party started, the skipper had the floor.

The tenor of the room stood in stark contrast to six days prior, when the Guardians fell into a 2-0 hole in the American League Division Series that put their season on the brink. This time, it would not be quiet for very long.

“Backs against the wall!” Vogt yelled. “Three straight elimination games! You boys showed up. You showed out. We've posted all year. No one counts us in. We’ve got eight more wins to go!”

Whether or not there was more to Vogt’s speech, the champagne shower that overtook the clubhouse made the call for him.

Cleveland was staring down the end of its 2026 campaign on Monday. Now, it’s four wins away from reaching the World Series. The Guardians beat the White Sox, 2-0, on Saturday to win the ALDS and secure a matchup against the Rays in the AL Championship Series that opens Monday night at Tropicana Field.

The Guardians did so with a comeback for the ages. They are the 11th team to lose the first two games of a best-of-five postseason series and then come back to win. They’re the first to do so since the 2017 Yankees, who pulled off the feat in Cleveland.

The Guards are the ninth to pull off the feat in the Division Series; two teams did it in the League Championship Series back when that had a best-of-five format.

“It's about resilience,” Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti said. “This group has demonstrated that time and time again throughout the course of the season. 

“With their backs against the wall, they never had any doubt and found a way to make it happen.”

Cleveland seems to play its best ball when adversity is at its highest. The Guardians pulled off a historic comeback en route to the AL Central title in 2025. These Guardians erased a 5 1/2-game deficit over the final six weeks of the regular season to track down the White Sox and win the division again. 

In this ALDS, the Guardians found a way to chase them down one more time. 

“We had a clear mindset, and we knew we could come back,” third baseman José Ramírez said through team interpreter Agustin Rivero. “We lost the first two games, but we knew we could come back in those three games. We knew we could come back and play our game, and we just had to understand that.”

The contributions of No. 11 were vital. Without him, the Guards may have already gone home for the winter.

Ramírez had a forgettable regular season marred by the left hamate surgery he underwent in June. He still is dealing with the impacts of that procedure, and it was fair to wonder what he would provide the Guardians once the calendar flipped to October.

Ramírez went 0-for-6 in Games 1 and 2, both of which Cleveland lost. He went 5-for-12 with a double, two homers and seven RBIs in the Guardians’ wins in Games 3-5. His two-run home run got Cleveland off and running on Saturday.

“If there's one person on the planet I would not doubt, it's José Ramírez,” Antonetti said. “He willed his way to finding a way to help us win these games.”

“It's a big time player,” Vogt said. “That's what guys going to Cooperstown do. They step up when they need to.”

“Build the [bleeping] statue,” reliever Erik Sabrowski said.

Saturday, of course, was a team-wide effort. Gavin Williams delivered a performance that will go down in franchise lore, racking up 12 strikeouts over 5 2/3 scoreless innings two days after he closed out Game 4 with an emergency relief appearance. Closer Cade Smith (who threw 50 pitches across Games 3 and 4) tossed 1 2/3 scoreless innings Saturday to earn the save.

# White Sox lose 2026 ALDS to Guardians

Author: Scott Merkin
Published: 2026-10-11T05:29:00Z
Source: mlb.com
Language: en

## Story

White Sox lose 2026 ALDS to Guardians
# White Sox magical season ends in Game 5 of ALDS: 'This team will be back'
12:29 AM CDT
Scott Merkin
CLEVELAND -- The White Sox clubhouse was what people would expect after their unexpected but highly entertaining 2026 season came to a close in the American League Division Series with a 2-0 loss to Cleveland during Game 5 on Saturday night at Progressive Field.
There were hugs. There were tears. There were smiles while thinking about the vast list of accomplishments, achieved individually and as a team. There was high hope for what could be on the horizon. White Sox chairman Jerry Reinsdorf made the point of greeting the team as they came off the field into said clubhouse, thanking them for this special campaign.
Yet, there was disappointment for what might have been, after the Guardians won the series, 3-2, by coming back to win the final three games following two opening losses at home.
“It was fun, but we didn’t want to end it here,” said White Sox second baseman Chase Meidroth, pausing to find the right words through his emotions. “They played a hell of a game. They pitched their asses off. They deserve to go to the next round. It sucks, but we’ll be back.”
“My intention was to win this game and fly to Tampa and play another series,” said White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami through interpreter Kenzo Yagi. “It’s really disappointing we lost. We are still a very young team. We have to learn from our experience here and then bring that to next year. But it’s disappointing.”
Saturday’s setback marked a strange ending for the White Sox, who never lost more than four in a row all season and only hit that mark twice. They lost three in a row on nine different occasions prior to Saturday’s loss.
This team topped the American League with 776 runs scored and 589 walks and sat third in home runs (211) and OPS (.726) over the 162-game regular season. But the swing-and-miss factor is what sent them home from Cleveland.
Gavin Williams came back to start Game 5 for Cleveland after throwing 18 pitches in the ninth inning Thursday to close out Game 4 at Rate Field. He struck out 12 over 5 2/3 innings in Game 5 and did not allow a hit until Kyle Teel’s single to right field with two outs in the sixth.
The White Sox only real rally came in that sixth when a walk to Miguel Vargas loaded the bases with two outs. Erik Sabrowski replaced Williams, and he struck out Murakami on five pitches.
Murakami fanned four times, as did Andrew Benintendi, as Cleveland pitchers notched 21 strikeouts in total, which is the most all-time in a nine-inning regular season or postseason game. The 75 White Sox strikeouts in the five-game series set a new LDS record.
“I thought it was less about chase and more about being attacked in the zone and swing and miss in the zone,” White Sox manager Will Venable said. “Just didn't have what it would have took to move some balls forward there. And I think, obviously, the story is just being able to put the ball in play.”
“They are a good baseball team,” said White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery of Cleveland. “It’s tough to beat someone three times in a row, and they dug deep and they did what they did. I feel like everybody assumed this series would go to the fifth game. It’s a good baseball team. They scrapped it out."
White Sox right-hander Sean Burke was solid but slightly less effective as the dominant Williams, yielding two runs over five innings. Those two came on a José Ramírez home run in the fourth on a pitch he basically took off the ground.
So, instead of moving on to the ALCS for the first time since ‘05, it was time to briefly reflect. The White Sox reached the Division Series with a two-game sweep of the Astros in the AL Wild Card Series. ## Cleveland pitchers set a nine-inning postseason record with 21 strikeouts against Chicago, rallying from an 0-2 hole to advance to Monday night's matchup at Tampa Bay.

 By AP 

 Oct 11, 2026 at 1:26 am ET • 5 min read 

CLEVELAND (AP) Gavin Williams and José Ramírez delivered when the Cleveland Guardians needed them the most.

Williams had 12 of a record 21 strikeouts by Cleveland pitchers, Ramírez hit a two-run, go-ahead home run on a pitch just above home plate in the fourth inning and the Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 Saturday night to complete a comeback from an 0-2 deficit in their best-of-five AL Division Series.

AL Central champion Cleveland became just the 11th team to win a best-of-five series among the 96 that fell behind 0-2, the first since the 2017 New York Yankees against the Cleveland Indians and only the fourth to achieve the feat after losing the first two games at home.

“I’d say that the confidence that we have in this group has been really tested and refined over the course of the last two years," Guardians closer Cade Smith said. “As a group, we’ve dealt with some adversity and seen us come out on the other side of that and had success in spite of that. And that builds a quiet foundation of confidence to play from.”

The Guardians open the AL Championship Series at Tampa Bay on Monday night, seeking their first World Series trip since 2016. Cleveland hasn’t won the title since 1948, the longest drought among MLB teams.

It will be an ALCS matchup of small-payroll teams. Cleveland started the season with the lowest in the major leagues and the Rays were 26th.

Chicago, the first team to reach the playoffs after three straight 100-loss seasons, won its first four postseason games, including a Wild Card Series sweep of Houston, then lost four in a row. The White Sox have not won the World Series since 2005.

“We are sitting in disappointment, and it hurts not to be able to advance," Chicago manager Will Venable said. "At the same time, you know, you do zoom out and look what this group accomplished and what they did to bring baseball back to White Sox and the pride back to the organization and then really the city.”

Guardians pitchers set a record for strikeouts in a nine-inning postseason game and the most in any nine-inning regular or postseason game since at least 1900. The White Sox got just three hits and put only nine balls in play.

“Our pitchers are incredible. We asked a ton of them this whole series,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. “When you miss bats, they can’t get anything going. And they just shut them down, and that’s a really good offense over there.”

Two days after saving Game 4, Williams became just the third pitcher in postseason history to get the last out of a game and start the following game when his team faced elimination in both.

The 27-year-old right-hander needed seven pitches in the first inning and struck out the side in the second and fifth.

“He can be that quiet guy, but he’s that silent killer. He’s going to go and do his best,” Ramírez said through an interpreter.

Chicago's only two baserunners came via a walk and hit by pitch until Kyle Teel looped a knuckle-curve into right field with two outs in the sixth.

“We got him out earlier than he wanted the other day - and he got us today. He was unbelievable and kept things out of the zone," Chicago second baseman Chase Meidroth said.

Williams had 24 strikeouts over three games, one shy of the mark for a best-of-five postseason series. His 12 Sunday tied Cleveland’s record for a postseason game set by Charles Nagy.

He got 22 swings and misses, throwing mostly curves and sweeps and firing 18 at 100 mph or higher Monday.

“I think that goes back to seeing them six or seven times now. And Patey (catcher Patrick Bailey) did a good job back there," Williams said. “He was reading swings the whole time.”

White Sox' season ends with 2-0 loss to Guardians in decisive Game 5 of ALDS - Chicago Sun-Times

## After leading the AL in runs per game this season, the Sox’ offense was silenced with an MLB postseason-record 21-strikeout performance against their division rivals.

 By James Fegan 

Sox hitting struck out 75 times over five games against Guardians pitching.

Nick Cammett/Getty

CLEVELAND — The unmistakable end-of-season sound of large men exchanging daps and bro hugs filled the visitors’ clubhouse late Saturday at Progressive Field.

‘‘This is my favorite team I’ve ever played on,’’ starting pitcher Sean Burke said after the Sox were eliminated from the postseason with a 2-0 loss to the Guardians in Game 5 of the American League Division Series.

By the time the media were allowed to enter the locker room of a Sox team with the youngest position-player group in the AL, there was a heaping supply of perspective about a magical season that defied the odds and portended more entertaining summers to come on the South Side.

‘‘We came into the year with a 0% chance of making the playoffs, and we shocked the world,’’ shortstop Colson Montgomery said. ‘‘Coming up short like this, it hurts. It hurts a lot. But there’s a lot to be proud of.’’

Elsewhere, eyelids were rimmed with red. The few veterans sprinkled among the youngsters know that life in professional baseball rarely feels as warm as it did this season, that next season isn’t guaranteed to be better and that getting within a victory of playing for the AL pennant is a missed opportunity.

‘‘It’s tough,’’ third baseman Miguel Vargas said. ‘‘We expected to win. They were better than us.’’

That the Sox split their regular-season and playoff matchups against the Guardians at nine victories apiece is cold comfort, if any at all. Both in the teams’ final regular-season series that swung the AL Central race and in overcoming a 2-0 deficit in the ALDS, the Guardians bested the Sox when it mattered.

‘‘We didn’t want to end it here,’’ dismayed second baseman Chase Meidroth said. ‘‘We had a good year, but we wanted better.’’

As much as the efforts to stretch Burke and a few high-leverage relievers dominated the attention through the Sox’ postseason run, it’s the way their offense — the most productive in the AL during the regular season — was shut down by the Guardians’ pitching staff in three consecutive losses to end the season that will linger.

After the Sox set an MLB postseason record for a nine-inning game with 19 strikeouts in Game 3, they broke it with 21 in Game 5. The Sox, who had the fifth-highest strikeout rate in the majors during the regular season, fanned 75 times in the series and homered only twice.

‘‘They did a lot of a lot of things well and exposed us in a lot of ways,’’ catcher Kyle Teel said. ‘‘We’ve just got to take a step back and look at how can we adjust for next year.’’

In their seventh encounter of the season against Guardians right-hander Gavin Williams, two days after he pitched the final inning of Game 4, he was the best many Sox players had seen him, striking out 12 batters in 5⅔ innings.

But as they did in each of his starts against them this season, the Sox chased Williams before he could complete six full innings. He departed with the bases loaded and two outs in the sixth.

With the Sox trailing 2-0 at the time, thanks to a simply miraculous home run by Jose Ramirez on a curveball from Burke no higher than his ankles in the fourth inning, the game was in the hands of slugger Munetaka Murakami in a matchup against Guardians left-hander Erik Sabrowski.

Randal Grichuk, who led the majors in slugging percentage against left-handed pitching, was available to pinch-hit. But for the Sox, who made much of their clubhouse believe postseason baseball was possible when they signed Murakami, the idea of taking the fate of the season out of his hands was a non-starter.

‘‘No, zero,’’ manager Will Venable said when asked if he considered pinch-hitting.

Guardians complete ALDS comeback, blank White Sox in Game 5 | Sports | The Daily News

# Guardians complete ALDS comeback, blank White Sox in Game 5 

- By Brian Dulik, Field Level Media
- Oct 10, 2026 
- Oct 10, 2026

 

 

 Oct 10, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez (11) celebrates the win with Cleveland Guardians pitcher Cade Smith (36) against the Chicago White Sox in game five of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images David Richard 

CLEVELAND -- Jose Ramirez hit a two-run homer and Gavin Williams struck out a franchise postseason-record-tying 12, leading the host Cleveland Guardians to a 2-0 victory over the Chicago White Sox in the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night.

Cleveland became the fourth team to win a best-of-five series after losing the first two games at home.

Erik Sabrowski, Hunter Gaddis and Cade Smith joined Williams in a combined three-hitter for the Guardians, who will meet the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series starting Monday in St. Petersburg, Fla.

Ramirez sent starter Sean Burke's knuckle curve 348 feet over the right-field wall, scoring Steven Kwan, who led off the fourth with the game's first hit. The 78 mph pitch was well below the strike zone, but Ramirez golfed it inside the foul pole, giving him seven RBIs over the final three games of the series.

Williams (1-0) carried a no-hitter into the sixth -- two days after recording the final three outs in Game 4 -- before Kyle Teel laced a two-out single. Williams, who had hit Colson Montgomery to open the sixth, walked Miguel Vargas after Teel's hit. Sabrowski entered and struck out Munetaka Murakami to end the inning.

Williams worked 5 2/3 innings, allowing one hit and walking two. The right- hander's 24 strikeouts over three appearances were one shy of the Division Series record set by Gerrit Cole of the Houston Astros in 2019.

Williams matched the Cleveland single-game postseason record of 12 strikeouts, set by Charles Nagy in the 1996 ALDS against the Baltimore Orioles. Williams owns two of the five double-digit strikeout performances in team playoff history.

# Williams' short-rest gem helps Guardians complete ALDS comeback

- Jesse Rogers Oct 11, 2026, 10:54 AM

Close

- Jesse joined ESPN Chicago in September 2009 and covers MLB for ESPN.com.

Follow on X

CLEVELAND -- The swings and misses kept coming for the Chicago White Sox on Saturday night -- one after the other, after the other.

It was part of a record-setting night for the Guardians' pitching staff, led by starter Gavin Williams, who fanned 12 in his 5⅔ innings in Cleveland's series-clinching 2-0 win in the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series.

The bullpen picked up where Williams left off, striking out nine more batters to push the Guardians' total to 21, an MLB record for any nine-inning game, regular season or postseason.

"Almost like nothing I've ever seen before," second baseman Travis Bazzana said. "Every pitch in the zone was a whiff. I couldn't believe it."

Neither could the White Sox, who struck out three times in four different innings, including in the ninth to set the record. The dominant pitching performance helped cap a dramatic series comeback for the Guardians, who are just the 11th team in 94 tries to win a best-of-five series after losing the first two games.

The Guardians will face the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series, with Game 1 on Monday.

"It's about resilience," Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti said during the champagne celebration after the win. "This group has demonstrated this time and time again."

No one showed more resiliency over the past few days than Williams and third baseman Jose Ramirez. Williams, pitching on a day's rest Saturday, showed increased velocity during his Game 5 outing and allowed just one hit.

Ramirez, who came up big this series after enduring an injury-plagued regular season, accounted for the only runs of Game 5. He took White Sox starter Sean Burke deep in the bottom of the fourth after connecting on a curveball just 0.89 feet from the ground. It was the lowest ball hit for a home run in the postseason since tracking began in 2008, and it added to Ramirez's growing Hall of Fame legacy in Cleveland.

"We've faced him a couple of times," Ramirez, speaking through the team interpreter, said of Burke. "So we know he has a really good curveball. So in that AB, I was looking for a curveball for strike."

Except it was far from a strike. It was at Ramirez's feet, and it came after four consecutive pitches at his eyes.

"I asked him how he hit that home run," Antonetti said with a laugh. "He said, 'It was a home run pitch. I was looking for it.'"

Pitching on a day's rest, Gavin Williams became first pitcher in MLB history with 12 or more strikeouts and one or fewer hits allowed in a winner-take-all postseason game. Phil Long/AP

Ramirez delivered exactly when the Guardians needed him most. After beginning the ALDS 0-for-6, Ramirez went 5-for-12 with two home runs over the past three games, carrying the team to victory.

"Build the f---ing statue," reliever Erik Sabrowski screamed of Ramirez's performance.

Of the Guardians pitchers' 21 strikeouts, Sabrowski got the biggest one. He was called on to protect a 2-0 lead against White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami with the bases loaded and two outs in the top of the sixth. He struck him out on five pitches.

"I think I threw the plan out the window and said f--- it," Sabrowski said. "I'm going to throw you fastballs."

It was one of four strikeouts for Murakami, who whiffed 11 times in the series. So did catcher Kyle Teel, who struck out twice Saturday. Andrew Benintendi also had four strikeouts Saturday, and Chase Meidroth had three.

Williams set the tone for the Guardians' pitchers after declaring he was ready to start Game 5 just two days after he recorded the last three outs of Game 4.

"I asked him how he hit that home run," Antonetti said with a laugh. "He said, 'It was a home run pitch. I was looking for it.'"
Ramirez delivered exactly when the Guardians needed him most. After beginning the ALDS 0-for-6, Ramirez went 5-for-12 with two home runs over the past three games, carrying the team to victory.
"Build the f---ing statue," reliever Erik Sabrowski screamed of Ramirez's performance.
Of the Guardians pitchers' 21 strikeouts, Sabrowski got the biggest one. He was called upon to protect a 2-0 lead against White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami with the bases loaded and two outs in the top of the sixth. He struck him out on five pitches.
"I think I threw the plan out the window and said f--- it," Sabrowski said. "I'm going to throw you fastballs."
It was one of four strikeouts for Murakami, who whiffed 11 times in the series. So did catcher Kyle Teel, who struck out twice Saturday. Andrew Benintendi also had four strikeouts Saturday, and Chase Meidroth had three.
Williams set the tone for the Guardians' pitchers after declaring he was ready to start Game 5 just two days after he recorded the last three outs of Game 4.
